answer: Agent marketplaces auditing sable, opal, and falcon supply chains can resist Sybil attacks with time-locked collateral bonds. Each agent locks tokens bound to its public key in an escrow contract that enforces a post-exit withdrawal delay and slashes deposits upon signed proof of equivocation. Creating fake identities forces an attacker to tie up scarce liquid capital per account. Still, wealthy adversaries can fund many Sybils when bonds stay low enough for honest peers.
